title: iRun Subic Bay 2026 Leg 3 Review: A Marathon-Only Finale at Remy Field
seo_title: iRun Subic Bay Leg 3 2026 Review | Zambales, PH
meta_description: iRun Subic Bay 2026 Leg 3 review: November 29 at Remy Field, Subic -- a marathon-only finale in the former US Naval Base Freeport Zone.
dek: Set for 29 November 2026 at Remy Field, this is the third and final leg of the iRun Subic Bay series -- a single-distance, 42.195K-only event in the former US Naval Base's Freeport Zone.
verdict: iRun Subic Bay Leg 3 is a genuinely focused event: the 42.195K full marathon only, no shorter categories at all, held at Remy Field within the Subic Bay Freeport Zone -- the same historically significant former US Naval Base area covered at the MILO Marathon's Subic leg elsewhere in this research batch. Organised by SMOKE10 Events, the same team behind the Isla del Fuego Marathon, Pampanga Marathon and Clark Phil-Kor Half Marathon covered elsewhere in this research, giving it credible operational backing even as a single-distance, less mainstream event.

sections.heading: The Series Finale, Marathon Only
paragraphs: iRun Subic Bay Leg 3 offers just one distance: the 42.195K full marathon, held at Remy Field in Subic, Zambales. [1] That single-distance format is genuinely unusual among the races covered in this research batch, most of which offer at least three or four categories -- this is a race for committed marathoners specifically, not a broad community event.

sections.heading: The Same Freeport Zone Covered Elsewhere
paragraphs: Subic Bay was formerly home to a major US Naval Base until the Navy's 1992 departure, since redeveloped into the Subic Bay Freeport Zone -- the same venue hosting the MILO Marathon's Subic leg covered elsewhere in this research batch. [2] Remy Field is a specific location within that broader Freeport Zone, giving the marathon a genuinely distinctive former-military backdrop.

sections.heading: An Established Organiser
paragraphs: SMOKE10 Events organises this race, the same team behind the Isla del Fuego Marathon on Siquijor, the long-running annual Pampanga Marathon, and the Clark Phil-Kor Half Marathon covered elsewhere in this research batch. [1] That multi-race track record across different Philippine destinations gives this Leg 3 event credible operational backing.

sections.heading: Registration Not Yet Announced, Being Leg 3
paragraphs: As of this writing, registration status has not been announced. [1] The 'Leg 3' naming implies this is part of a multi-race iRun Subic Bay series, though specific details about the earlier legs weren't found in available research.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want a focused, marathon-only event in the historically significant Subic Bay Freeport Zone, run by an organiser with genuine track record across multiple Philippine races, iRun Subic Bay Leg 3 on 29 November 2026 is a solid pick for committed marathoners.
